==History==
===Entering League of Legends and the LJL (2019)===
After the [[Unsold Stuff Gaming]] team didn't renew its contract with LJL at the end of the 2019 Season for the next franchise year, the Fukuoka SoftBank HAWKS gaming, a subsidiary of the [[wikipedia:Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks|Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks baseball team]] who is playing at the [[wikipedia:Nippon Professional Baseball|Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB)]] as a member of the [[wikipedia:Pacific League|Pacific League]], was chosen to enter the LJL franchise.

===A tough year (2020)===
In their first season (2020), the first-ever roster of the team was formed by Korean Top laner Kim "[[DasheR]]" Deok-beom, Korean Jungler Lee "[[Tussle]]" Moon-yong (recognized as a Japanese resident by Interregional Movement Policy (IMP) from Riot), Japanese/Chinese Mid laner Osamu "[[Ramune]]" Ozawa, Korean Bottom laner Park "[[Honey]]" Bo-heon, and the Japanese Support Norimitsu "[[Pooh]]" Hosogai, with Naoya "[[Arumik]]" Kimura being the substitute. That team finished the season with just 8th position in the [[LJL/2020/Spring|Spring Split]] and 5th-6th in the [[LJL/2020/Summer|Summer Split]], when they lost to Crest Gaming Act 3:1 in the first round of Playoffs.

===Grounded (2021)===
For the 2021 season, Ramune, Honey,  Pooh, Arumik and [[Awaker]] left the team to Ryo "[[apaMEN]]" Odagiri, Jeon "[[Zenit]]" Tae-gwon, Australian/Japanese Ian "[[Corporal]]" Pearse, and Park "[[Squirtle]]" Hyeon-woo arrived. Plus, DasheR changed his position from Top to Mid lane and Coach [[Sweet]] changed from Coach to Head Coach. But they were eliminated twice again in their first round of Playoffs to V3 Esports ([[LJL/2021/Spring|Spring]] 3:2, [[LJL/2021/Summer|Summer]]Summer 3:0).

===Big Changes (2022)===
Big changes occurred for the 2022 season when apaMEN announced his retirement from LoL Pro scene; Corporal, Zenit and Coaches Squirtle and Sweet left the team. In addition, Tussle changed his function as a player to be the Coach of the team with the Korean Head Coach Kim "[[Ares]]" Min-kwon. The new roster was formed by: Top laner Yuto "[[Kinatu]]" Enomoto, former [[https://liquipedia.net/overwatch/Luna_(Japanese_player)|Overwatch player]] and Bottom laner Rei "[[Marble]]" Shimaya, two Japanese promises of Japan scene. Jungler Blank, previously [[SK Telecom T1|SKT Telecom T1 player]] and Worlds champion in [[World Championship/2016|2016]], DasheR, and Japanese Support Shin "[[Raina]]" Okubo, LJL Champion in [[LJL/2020/Summer|2020]] with [[V3 Esports]].  One more time, in the [[LJL/2022/Spring|Spring Split]], they were eliminated in the First round of Playoffs for [[Burning Core]], but in the [[LJL/2022/Summer|Summer]] they got to the Semifinals when lost to [[Sengoku Gaming]] 3:1 in a one-sided series.

===A Great Year (2023)===
Oh "[[Vsta]]" Hyo-seong arrived for the 2023 season to replace Raina. In the [[LJL/2023/Spring|Spring Split]], SHG lost to [[DetonatioN FocusMe]] 3:0 after playing against them for the their first time in the LJL Playoffs, this loss resulted in a 3rd-4th place. In the [[LJL/2023/Summer|Summer Split]], SHG became the second force in the league facing DFM two more times during Playoffs when lost to them at the Upper Bracket Finals 3:2 and at the Grand Finals (the first offline LJL Finals since 2019) 3:2 for DFM again.
